title: The Two-Candy Revolt: Exit Is Not Leverage
scope: Synthetic computational mechanism study; no LLM calls or human subjects. Not a reconstruction of the missing original training program.

baseline.finite: Enumerate all 3003 count allocations, optimum, individual equilibria, and role rotation.
baseline.new_learning: Four reward functions; 64 independent seeds; 12000 rounds; ten epsilon-greedy bandit learners per group; observed personal reward EMA; shared reward divided by ten. This is a fresh algorithm, not an exact replication of the prior chat claims.
baseline.evaluation: 2000 new lottery rounds with frozen greedy policies and uniform tie-breaking

bargaining.description: The eight-candy agent offers an integer transfer 0..8 to the two-candy agent. Eight bystanders keep 33 candies. This deliberately reduced game tests a prerequisite for the proposed ten-agent society, not autonomous institution invention.
bargaining.no_refusal: The receiver must accept; the outside option is unavailable.
bargaining.exit_only: Rejection leaves proposer with 8 and receiver with outside option; bystanders keep 33. Receiver's porch produces no candy.
bargaining.veto: Rejection additionally cancels the proposer's 8-candy payout. This is an explicit institutional intervention, not a property of the original independent porches.
bargaining.escrow: Accepted offers are automatically executed and conserve candy.
bargaining.unenforced: Proposer chooses an offer and an honor/renege bit together; receiver observes the offer but not the bit. This is a deliberately hidden-action game, not natural-language deception or spontaneous invention of dishonesty.
bargaining.private_rewards: Each strategic agent's own realized candy, including outside supply on rejection.
bargaining.shared_rewards: Sum of all ten realized bags including outside supply, divided by ten; no inequity penalty or fairness bonus.
bargaining.learner: Independent one-step tabular action-value learning, learning rate 0.05. Proposer observes no state; receiver conditions on the numerical offer. No memory of counterpart actions except through learned values; no language or reputation ledger.
bargaining.evaluation: Exact expected metrics of frozen greedy policies plus 600 fresh sampled rounds (20 nominal 30-night seasons). No update during evaluation.
bargaining.pairing: Common random numbers within each seed across all 24 cells; seeds are independent.
bargaining.inference: Mean and 95% seed-bootstrap intervals; seed is the replication unit, not individual rounds; descriptive exploratory pilot, no confirmatory p-values.
bargaining.stress_test: For outside-option-zero policies only, run 30 adaptive nights with epsilon 0.05; outside option becomes 3 on nights 11..20 then reverts. Paired no-shock control. Report as short nonstationary stress test, not durable institution evidence.

hypotheses: In the exit-only personal-reward game, zero transfer is weakly dominant for proposer: exit alone cannot create a material incentive to compensate.
A veto with a credible outside option can elicit compensation without any fairness reward; equality is not implied.
Unenforced promises can undermine compensation; learning may cycle or fail to converge rather than reach a simple equilibrium.
Shared reward can leave distribution underdetermined even when production is high.
planned_robustness: Repeat bargaining with learning rates 0.02 and 0.10, 32 seeds each, 12000 rounds. Run an escrow private-reward exact best-response receiver control to distinguish game incentives from learning failure.
records: Persist source, protocol hash, every training offer/acceptance/reward, initial/final values, periodic checkpoints, exact and sampled evaluation, per-seed metrics, shock trajectories, test receipts, and hashes. No selective removal of seeds.
